title.narrative: Sustainable and Inclusive Economic Recovery Program, Subprogram 1

description.narrative: The program will help the Government of Kiribati implement reforms to support inclusive and sustainable recovery following the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic. It will be financed through two policy-based grants of $5 million each, delivered through subprogram 1 (November 2021-August 2023) and subprogram 2 (September 2023-December 2024). A programmatic approach will allow for sequencing and deepening of policy reforms to account for limited implementation capacity, and provide flexibility to respond to unforeseen constraints or opportunities. Subprogram 1 introduces new policies and legal and regulatory frameworks to (i) reduce macro fiscal risks by strengthening public financial management (PFM) and fiscal sustainability, including for state-owned enterprises (SOEs); (ii) improve the enabling environment for private sector development by strengthening the finance sector and increasing female labor force participation through reduced gender-based violence (GBV); and (iii) enhance protection of the environment and natural resources for more sustainable and inclusive growth. Subprogram 2 will build on these foundations and help implement, deepen, and institutionalize reforms. The program builds on reforms supported through the past programs and ongoing technical assistance (TA) of the Asian Development Bank (ADB). The program was developed in collaboration with the European Union, the governments of Australia and New Zealand, and the World Bank.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

1.1. To improve public financial management and transparency: (i) The Cabinet approved, and MFED published on their website in December 2022, the Fiscal Reporting Policy, which sets out new standard processes and timelines for regular public financial reporting, improving transparency and aligning government financial reporting with international standards; and includes a sequenced transition plan; and (ii) The Accountant General approved effective September 2022, and the Treasury and Budget division at MFED began implementing, a new Chart of Accounts consistent with the Government Finance Statistics and International Public Sector Accounting Standards.

1.2. To strengthen public financial management data quality and reporting, MFED procured an IFMIS and a service provider that meets identified requirements in June 2022, and commenced IFMIS implementation.
1.3. To increase tax revenues through improved tax administration and tax compliance, in February 2023 the cabinet submitted to Parliament for enactment an Income Tax Bill.

1.4. To improve SOEs monitoring and financial management: (i) 12 (of 18) SOEs tabled their 2023 SOI to Parliament by December 2022 in compliance with statutory reporting requirements; and (ii) MFED approved new model accountability documents for SOE monitoring including SOIs and Annual Reports in January 2023, effective immediately.

1.5. To improve financial supervision and promote soundness of the financial system in Kiribati, in December 2021 Parliament approved, and in April 2023 Minister MFED commenced implementation of the Financial Supervisory Authority of Kiribati Act that covers the establishment, powers, governance, and operation of the supervisory authority.

1.6. To maintain the quality of governance of financial institutions and protect the soundness of the financial system, in December 2021, Parliament approved, and in April 2023 Minister MFED issued a commencement notice for the Kiribati Financial Institutions Act.

1.7. To increase female workforce participation, effective 31 August 2023, the cabinet approved a national policy to Eliminate Sexual and Gender-based Violence 2023-2038 and an accompanying 5-year implementation plan.

1.8. To reduce environmental degradation and protect and conserve Kiribati's ecosystems, the Parliament approved in November 2021 the Environment Act, and in August 2022 Minister, MELAD issued a commencement notice for the Act, including provisions for (i) waste management, pollution control, and promotion of recycling and reuse, (ii) setting up and enforcement of environmental standards to control environmentally sensitive activities, (iii) protection and sustainable management of biological diversity; (iv) promotion of carbon reporting, and (v) increasing access to environment data to facilitate evidence-based decision making

1.9. To ensure long term conservation of Kiribati's fisheries, in December 2021 Parliament approved an amendment to the Fisheries Act 2010 to include preservation of biological diversity and conservation of all marine resources within the Act's purview.

2.1. To improve public financial management and transparency: (i) MFED will publish fiscal reports consistent with the Fiscal Reporting Policy, including quarterly budget performance reports, annual public procurement report and RERF report (ii) The Cabinet will approve and submit to Parliament for enactment a new PFM bill to implement a new PFM legal framework consistent with the Fiscal Reporting Policy; and (iii) MFED will conduct a PEFA assessment including a Climate and Gender Responsiveness Module, and begin a phased implementation of its recommendations.

2.2. To strengthen public financial management data quality and reporting, MFED will implement all four modules of the new IFMIS, including revenue and expenditure, debt and grant monitoring, fixed asset management and e-procurement modules.
2.3. To increase tax revenues, the cabinet will approve and the Tax division at MFED will publish and implement regulations of the Income Tax Act.

2.4. To improve SOE monitoring and financial management: (i) At least 15 (out of 18) SOEs will table their SOIs before Parliament in compliance with statutory reporting and model document requirements introduced in subprogram 1. (ii) At least 5 (of 18) SOEs will table their Annual Reports (inclusive of audited financial statements) in Parliament in compliance with statutory reporting and model document requirements.
2.5. To implement the Financial Supervisory Authority of Kiribati Act, the government will operationalize the Financial Supervisory Authority by appointing a CEO, board members and dedicated staff.
2.6. Government will approve prudential regulations to be implemented by the Financial Supervisory Authority of Kiribati.

2.7. To improve female workforce participation, MWYSSA will operationalize a central database that compiles information on GBV disaggregated by nature of case, age, gender and disability as part of the 5-year implementation plan.

2.8. To reduce environmental degradation and protect and conserve Kiribati's ecosystems, (i) the Cabinet will approve and the MELAD will implement regulations of the Environment Act 2021 including on solid waste management. (ii) MFED will increase the coverage of the Special Fund for Recycling under the Special Fund Act, to include end of life vehicles, tires, laptops, and phones; so that deposits are refunded when the items are delivered to a recycling depot.

2.9. To ensure long term conservation of Kiribati's fisheries, the cabinet will approve and the Ministry of Fisheries and Marine Resources Development will implement amended regulations on coastal fishing and aquaculture aligned with the amended Fisheries Act 2010.
